vectors.name: formats-toml/basic/array-of-tables-becomes-repeated-edges
vectors.comment: [[x]] is TOML's idiomatic repeated record and lands on the repeated-label shape with no adjustment needed -- of the four non-native formats, TOML's own idiom already matches the Document model.

vectors.name: formats-toml/temporals/native-date-time-and-datetime-all-resolve-with-no-schema
vectors.comment: TOML is the one format with native literals for all three temporal kinds -- and, unlike YAML, a bare time-of-day resolves correctly to `time` rather than a sexagesimal integer. Confirmed live.

vectors.name: formats-toml/nulls/null-leaf-cannot-be-written-and-is-omitted
vectors.comment: TOML has no null; the leaf cannot be written, so it's dropped and reported as a write-time adjustment rather than inventing a representation. Confirmed live the write still succeeds (see omnist-spec#28 for an open severity-classification question this vector deliberately doesn't assert on, since Sec8.5.2's diagnostics matching compares only path+code, never severity).

vectors.name: formats-toml/nulls/strict-mode-refuses-to-write-instead-of-omitting
vectors.comment: The non-strict companion vector (formats-toml/nulls/null-leaf-cannot-be-written-and-is-omitted) drops the value and reports format.null-unrepresentable, still succeeding. In strict mode the same value refuses the write entirely rather than silently adjusting -- confirmed live via --strict.
